# Results -- Study 263 (Insider-Buying) on the curated tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: pair a curated
monthly aggregate insider buy/sell ratio (open-market Form-4 purchases / sales) with
S&P 500 (^GSPC) **price-only** monthly returns; test whether a HIGH ratio (insiders
buying) forecasts the NEXT month's return via (a) a HAC predictive regression, (b) a
low/mid/high tercile sort, and (c) a long/flat timing overlay vs buy-and-hold.
**The buy/sell ratio is a CURATED PROXY, not a live Form-4 feed** (see
[`insider_buying/data.py`](../insider_buying/data.py)); the Signal axis is therefore
capped at WEAK by construction -- and the realised t-stat puts it lower still.
As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (ratio) |
|--------|--------|-------|---------------------|
| Curated insider buy/sell ratio (monthly) | 2003-01 -> 2025-12 | 276 months | `cc2e80f98d69` |
| ^GSPC monthly close (yfinance, price-only) | 2002-12 -> 2026-06 | 283 months | -- |

Merged analysis panel: **276 monthly observations** (275 with a forward return).
Price-only: the ~1.8%/yr S&P dividend yield is excluded from every level/return.

## Primary specification -- predictive regression (next-month return on standardised ratio)

| Coefficient | Value | HAC *t* | R^2 | n |
|-------------|-------|---------|-----|---|
| Slope (return per +1sigma of ratio) | **+0.0017/mo** | **+0.49** | 0.002 | 275 |

The slope is statistically indistinguishable from zero (HAC *t* = **+0.49**). The
buy/sell ratio explains **0.2%** of next-month return variance. There is **no
forecasting power** at the one-month aggregate horizon on this tape.

## Tercile sort -- next-month return by ratio bucket

| Ratio bucket | Next-month return (ann.) | HAC *t* | n |
|--------------|--------------------------|---------|---|
| Low (insiders selling) | +10% /yr | +3.6 | 92 |
| Mid | +13% /yr | +3.1 | 91 |
| **High (insiders buying)** | **+8% /yr** | +1.1 | 92 |
| **High minus Low** | **-3% /yr** | -- | 184 |

The contrarian story predicts high-ratio months should be FOLLOWED by *higher*
returns. They are not -- high-buying months are followed by slightly *lower* returns
(high-minus-low = **-3%/yr**, wrong sign). The signal is a non-event.

## Where the kernel of truth lives -- contemporaneous, not predictive

| Correlation | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| ratio vs **same-month** S&P return | **-0.083** |
| ratio vs **next-month** S&P return | +0.042 |

Insiders *do* buy more in down months (the negative contemporaneous correlation is
the documented "buy the dip" reflex). But that information is **coincident, not
predictive** -- by the time you observe the buying, the down move has already
happened, and the next month is a coin flip.

## Sub-period persistence -- predictive regression HAC *t*

| Period | Slope/mo | HAC *t* | n |
|--------|----------|---------|---|
| 2003--2010 | +0.0037 | +0.53 | 96 |
| 2011--2017 | -0.0060 | -1.69 | 84 |
| 2018--2025 | +0.0042 | +0.90 | 95 |

No sub-period clears *t* = 2; the middle period even flips sign. Nothing stable here.

## Tradability -- long/flat timing overlay vs buy-and-hold

The overlay goes LONG when the ratio is above its trailing 24-month median
(look-ahead-free) and FLAT otherwise, switching ~10% of months. One-way cost x NAV
on every switch.

| Spec | Mean return (ann.) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* | Max DD |
|------|--------------------|-------------|---------|--------|
| Overlay, net @ 5 bps one-way | **+3.4%/yr** | +0.28 | +1.22 | -50% |
| Overlay, net @ 10 bps | +3.3%/yr | +0.28 | +1.20 | -50% |
| Overlay, gross | +3.5%/yr | +0.29 | -- | -- |
| **Buy-and-hold (always long)** | **+10.2%/yr** | **+0.70** | -- | -53% |

The overlay sits flat ~55% of the time and therefore captures only a third of the
S&P's return, with a barely-better drawdown. **Buy-and-hold dominates by ~6.8pp/yr.**
There is no tradable edge.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds the signal when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`), the same regression
recovers a planted contrarian beta:

| Planted beta | Regression HAC *t* |
|--------------|--------------------|
| 0.00 (null)  | **-0.53** (~0) |
| +0.06        | **+3.17** |

The engine is truthful: it reads ~0 on the null and fires (t > 3) when a real effect
is planted. The curated real tape has nothing like it.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Predictive HAC *t* = **+0.49**; tercile high-minus-low is the
  *wrong sign* (-3%/yr); no sub-period clears *t* = 2. The documented insider reflex
  ("buy the dip") shows up *contemporaneously* (ratio vs same-month return = -0.08)
  but carries no one-month-ahead information. Independently, the buy/sell ratio is a
  **curated proxy**, which caps the axis at WEAK regardless of any t-stat -- but the
  realised statistics put it squarely at **NONE**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The long/flat overlay returns +3.4%/yr net vs +10.2%/yr
  for buy-and-hold; it sits in cash through more than half the sample and misses the
  upside. No vehicle, no edge.
- **Survivorship -- named.** The S&P 500 is a survivor index; the timing overlay
  does not select stocks, so the bias is mild, but it is named on the Signal axis.

> **Honesty note.** A REAL stamp would require a robust HAC *t* >= 2 on a *real*
> Form-4 tape. This study ships a curated proxy and a transparently null result; the
> literature (Lakonishok-Lee, Seyhun) finds modest aggregate power at 6-12 months,
> not at the one-month horizon tested here -- so the literature reads WEAK, the tape
> reads NONE, and we record NONE.
